findings.finding: BJ's direct competitor Sam's Club reported the SAME Aug-Oct quarter on 2026-11-19: US comp ex fuel +4.9% (Q2: +4.4%), transactions +5.1%. Costco's US comp ex gas ran 5.6% (Aug), 8.0% (Sep) and 8.1% (Oct), about 7.3% for BJ's quarter against 7.2% in Costco's May-Aug Q4, when BJ printed 3.1%. The club channel was stable to accelerating, against a street bar for BJ of 2.5% (BofA) to 3% (Zacks) and an easy 1.8% compare from last year's Q3.
findings.link: Same channel and format: Sam's and Costco are the two other US membership warehouse clubs, overlapping BJ's East Coast/Southeast/Texas footprint. Sam's numbers cover the identical Aug-Oct quarter (Walmart Q3 ended 2026-10-31; BJ Q3 ended ~2026-11-01).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BJ trades on comp ex gas. Q1 FY26 comp 1.5% gave -8.25%. Q2 FY26 comp 3.1% plus a raise gave +5.61%. Q3 FY25 comp 1.8% with an EPS beat gave +1.13% (baseline; company 8-Ks).
findings.why_not_priced: Sam's printed this morning, the day before BJ, and street comp estimates (2.5-3%) were set before it and sit below BJ's own Q2 rate. If priced, previews would quote a comp above 3%. They quote 2.5-3%.
findings.independence: Costco October sales release, a different company and document (https://www.morningstar.com/news/globe-newswire/9870370/costco-wholesale-corporation-reports-october-sales-results, 2026-11-04; August: https://www.rttnews.com/3688055/costco-net-sales-comps-rise-in-august-q4.aspx). findings.finding: Gasoline over BJ's Q3 was mostly a rising-price quarter: the AAA national average went from ~$4.10 in early Sept to a record $4.48 on 2026-09-24 (crude ~$100, Strait of Hormuz), then eased only to $4.22 by 2026-10-29. Murphy USA's Jul-Sep retail fuel margin was 27.4 cpg against 28.3 a year earlier, and same-store gallons were +0.1%. BJ's Q2 fuel outperformance came from a 'pullback from peak gas prices', so Q3 fuel profit per gallon is likely below Q2's outsized level and the EPS beat likely smaller than Q2's 16%.
findings.link: Murphy USA is a high-volume, price-led US fuel retailer, the same business as BJ's gas stations. The retail fuel margin is the line BJ credited for the Q2 beat and raise. No shared customer or revenue figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gas profit drove the Q2 FY26 beat and raise, and the stock went +5.61%. No other quarter's fuel line has been isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. TIKR and others already expect fuel to 'normalize', and EPS consensus is +6-9% y/y, not the +19% of Q2. If fully priced, the whisper would sit at or below consensus. It sits 4 cents above, so some of the Q2 fuel windfall is still expected.
findings.independence: AAA weekly releases (https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-dips-following-record-setting-september/, 2026-10-01; https://gasprices.aaa.com/news/page/3?lv=true). Murphy's 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001573516/000157351626000193/exh991_09302026er.htm. Macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by BJ.

findings.finding: Retail gasoline has fallen fast since BJ's quarter closed: AAA $4.22 (2026-10-29), $4.10 (11-05), $3.90 (11-12), $3.72 (11-19), as crude fell from >$100 to the high $80s and lower. Pump prices falling behind wholesale is the setup in which retail fuel margins widen. That gives a Q4 fuel-profit tailwind in the line management credited for the August raise, and supports a FY EPS guide above $4.60-4.80. Q4 needs only ~$1.00-1.06 against $0.96 last year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FY26 FY EPS raise on gas outperformance got +5.61%. Q3 FY25 (2025-11-21) also raised the FY outlook, with an EPS beat and a soft comp, and got +1.13%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street FY (~$4.70) sits at the guide midpoint, so no Q4 fuel windfall is in it. If priced, FY estimates would have moved above $4.80 in November. Zacks shows only +1 cent in 7 days and Investing.com +1.6% in 60 days.
findings.independence: Mechanism from the BLS note on rising/falling margins (https://www.bls.gov/opub/btn/volume-4/as-crude-oil-plunges-retail-gasoline-margins-spike-then-retreat.htm). Company basis: the 8-K of 2026-08-21 credits gas for the raise. Proxy: BJ has not confirmed Q4 fuel margins.

findings.finding: Merchandise margin funding thins in Q3. Management said the tariff refunds that funded H1 price cuts are 'nearly exhausted' going into the back half; Q2 merch margin was already -20bp y/y with the refunds. In Q3 BJ ran a 42%-off anniversary event (2026-09-24 to 10-31) across dozens of items. Replacement funding (supplier money, retail media, gas) is unproven, and Earnings Whispers frames -10 to -20bp as fine and worse as traffic bought at rising cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 merch margin -50bp (8-K 2026-03-05) got -1.51%. Q2 FY26 merch margin -20bp, offset by fuel, got +5.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: previews flag it, but nobody quantifies the merch margin, and the EPS consensus rising into the print suggests no margin step-down is modelled. If priced, Q3 EPS estimates would have been cut since August. They rose 1.6%.
findings.independence: Promo: BJ's Business Wire 2026-09-22 (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260922406849/en/BJs-Wholesale-Club-Celebrates-42-Years-of-Delivering-Unbeatable-Value-By-Delivering-Even-More-Value). Q2 margin: company 8-K 2026-08-21. Shares the 'refunds nearly exhausted' theme with the Earnings Whispers preview, counted once here.

findings.finding: Q2's $1.36 EPS beat (the base of the +18% run) was helped by a sale-leaseback gain that offset SG&A growth and was not adjusted out (adjusted EPS = GAAP EPS). Absent a similar gain in Q3, the y/y EPS growth comparison is tougher than Q2's +19% headline suggests.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated in any prior reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The gain was disclosed in August and consensus Q3 EPS growth of 6-9% is well below Q2's 19%, so this is largely in the bar. It matters only if the Q3 beat is read against Q2's quality.
findings.independence: Company Q2 8-K (adjusted = GAAP, no adjustments): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001531152/000153115226000053/bj-2026080126x8kex991.htm. Same document family, counted once.

findings.finding: Walmart launched a combined Walmart+ / Sam's Club Plus membership for $120 a year on 2026-10-20, against nearly $400 separately. Management said on 2026-11-19 it drew 'a couple million new members' in its first month, and Sam's is investing in fresh-food price. This is a new competitive pressure on BJ's membership acquisition and Club+ upgrades (BJ's Club+ is $120 alone) heading into Q4. BJ's FY guide and narrative were set before it existed.
findings.link: Direct substitute: a Sam's Club Plus membership competes for the same warehouse-club member. BJ's Club+ fee is also $120. No overlap figure is available.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BJ's membership fee hike (2024) was bought. No prior reaction to a competitor's membership pricing is on record here.
findings.why_not_priced: Uptake numbers became public only this morning. BJ's previews discuss MFI slowing from lapping its own fee hike, not a competitor bundle. If priced, previews would mention the bundle. None found does.
findings.independence: none (single transcript). Effect on BJ is inference; BJ has not commented.

findings.finding: Capital: on 2026-09-14 BJ committed to an investment-grade policy (net debt/LTM adj EBITDA below 1.0x, a move to an unsecured structure), and S&P lifted its outlook to positive on 2026-10-27. $422.1M of buyback authorization remained after Q2. Leverage headroom keeps buybacks going, so a refreshed authorization or upgrade commentary on the call is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2024 fee hike plus a large buyback announcement was bought (Kiplinger). Nothing since.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: public for two months. Only a new authorization would be news.
findings.independence: S&P outlook headline cited in the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-15 (https://finviz.com/news/422853/...).

findings.finding: Expansion: Earnings Whispers reports the Texas clubs running more than 30% ahead of plan. BJ opened Foley AL (2026-09-25), a second Kentucky club and Waxahachie TX in Q3/Q4, with seven openings plus one relocation planned for H2. New-club sales help total revenue but not the comp, and pre-opening costs weigh on SG&A, which roughly nets the item.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the opening count is guided. The 30%-ahead-of-plan claim is from management commentary already public.
findings.independence: Investing.com 2026-11-19 (Texas: 95% member renewal intent, five clubs open).

baseline_tension: The peer comp and November gas evidence point up, while the run-up, the above-target price, the Citi 'priced in' downgrade and short covering say a beat is expected. With no skew available and a 1.44 put/call OI ratio, the option market gives no clear direction, so the evidence nets to a coin flip and p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a proxy): the November gasoline / Q4 guide finding was cut from +1.2 to +0.9 and the Q3 fuel-margin finding from -0.5 to -0.4. Both are inferred from AAA and Murphy USA, not from a BJ number.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism': the 10b5-1 insider sales were cut from -0.1 to -0.05 and the short-covering item from -0.2 to -0.1, since neither carries company information.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): three EPS consensus sources agree within 3 cents, so no cap was applied. The stale Earnings Whispers FY $4.53 is rejected in favour of $4.70.

Lesson 1/7 (reaction vs fact, positioning): the expectations finding was left at -1.5. p_up stays at 50 and the expected move at 0. The sum (-1.35) and the scaled number disagree in sign because the positives are proxies and the negative is the price itself.
